chapter: Larry Shields and the Dixieland Band
title: Larry's marching bands and Clem Camp
summary: Harry says Laine gave many players their start, and tells of Larry in marching bands and the St. Francis de Sales Band with clarinetist Clem Camp.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Well, I imagine Jack just about gave all these guys their first start in the music business. And of course I've had quite a few to tell me that, such as Nick LaRocka, Larry. But Larry played with quite a few bands around here before he left, he played with the marching bands, you know, and played with Joe Ella Bush. I remember he had his conductor's cap and he just changed the name of the band, you know, and just put it over the cap and drive it. And I have a picture taken in 1907 when Larry played with the St. Francis de Sales Band. I have that picture at home. He and Clem Camp. Do you remember Clem? Did you ever hear of him? I think he's still living.
He's one of the old timers. I imagine now he's... Clem Camp. Clem Camp. I imagine he's in his 70s now. He lives somewhere on Talladonna near Galvis. I think he's still alive.
Yeah. Yeah. And he's one of the old timers.
And he and Larry played in that St. Francis de Sales Band together. And I don't know if Clem ever went away and left New Orleans.
